notes:
Summary: Large fintech platform building an enterprise code assistant for internal developer productivity (trading apps + risk tools). Primary needs: sub-100ms token tail latency for in-IDE streaming completion, per-model version pinning for compliance, immutable audit logs for generated code, SSO/SAML + SCIM, and configurable retention windows. Preferred architecture: private control plane in Redwood + on-prem inference agents inside their VPC for sensitive workloads.

Discovery notes (informal):
- Interested in Redwood Private first but wants Dedicated for non-sensitive teams.
- "We cannot risk model updates changing generated logic without review. Need model pinning and rollout audit trails." — Head of Dev Productivity.
- Concern: HSM/KMS integration for signing and key lifecycle. Procurement asked for annual TCO and runbook for data deletion.
- Wants streaming completions integrated with VS Code extension that uses local agent; latency SLO 50-100ms median, 200ms p95 for char-by-char streaming.

POC scope agreed:
- Week 0: network scoping + SSO test account.
- Week 1-2: deploy private control plane + single on-prem agent inside dev VPC.
- Week 3: integrate KMS & audit log export to SIEM.
- Week 4: run internal eval (devs use VS Code extension), collect latency/cost metrics and qualitative feedback.

Stated constraints: must pass security checklist v2 and internal vendor risk assessment. Data residency: primary US, some EU tenants must be isolated. Retention: code generation logs retained 2 years, but request ability to shorten for specific repos.

Quote snippets / call fragments:
- "If we can't pin models at service level we won't move forward."
- "Auditability is non-negotiable — compliance needs immutable traces."

Open artifacts: security FAQ (drive link), initial network diagram (pending), procurement request for pricing band (submitted).

AE notes / quick wins: prioritize HSM/KMS PoC and SSO single tenant setup; provide sample retention config and model-pinning demo; prepare cost sensitivity breakdown (dedicated vs private).
